brand_dna.category: Patented urinary bag covers for catheter and leg bag users - a discretion-and-dignity lane within medical device accessories.
brand_dna.core_belief: That people managing urinary devices deserve functionality and dignity: 'We are dedicated to creating products that empower individuals, where other products hold them back.'
proof_points: Crafted from durable, lightweight nylon with superior workmanship
Founder-invented in 2012 after a family member's post-cancer catheter experience
Used in both institutional and home care settings
brand_dna.positioning: Purpose-built, higher-quality alternative to the flimsy supplied bag holders - designed with the end user in mind, not a generic accessory.

icp: Adults living with urinary incontinence or catheters - plus their families and caregivers - who value discretion, comfort, and independence and want a dependable, dignified alternative to the flimsy supplied bag holder.

personas.name: The Independent User
personas.description: A catheter or leg bag user who wants to go about daily life confidently; moved by discretion, comfort, and 'a walk in the park' normalcy.

personas.name: The Caring Family Member
personas.description: A spouse or adult child sourcing a better solution after supplied gear failed; moved by dignity, reliability, and the founder's own family story.

personas.name: The Care Professional
personas.description: A nurse, caregiver, or facility buyer serving patients in home or institutional settings; moved by durability, washability, and secure fit.

allowed.claim: US Patented urinary bag covers designed for discretion, comfort, and security.
Crafted from durable, lightweight nylon and washable, wash-after-wash.
LEGG-INS fits most 19 oz (562 cc) urinary leg bags with adjustable straps for thigh or calf.
BAG-INS includes a removable dowel rod that helps the bag maintain shape and reduces tubing kinks.
Products are used in both institutional and home care settings.
Satisfaction guarantee - reach out directly if dissatisfied for any reason.

banned.why: Medical/therapeutic claim - the product is a cover, not a treatment device.

banned.claim: 'Prevents infection' or 'improves hygiene outcomes' as a health promise.
banned.why: Medical claim not supported by evidence on the site; blog hygiene mentions are not proof.
FTC Green Guides - unqualified sustainability claim with no verifiable backing.
FTC Green Guides - specific green claims require verifiable proof not present on the site.

banned.claim: 'Ensures consistent urine flow' stated as a guaranteed medical outcome.
banned.why: Reframe as design intent, not a clinical guarantee - avoid implied medical efficacy.
Copy only says it addresses concerns like allergic reactions; an absolute claim is unproven.
